newsitem.title: USA: U.S. spot resids steady to down, USG supported.
newsitem.headline: U.S. spot resids steady to down, USG supported.

text.p: U.S. spot fuel oil prices were steady to down slightly Wednesday in moderate trade, with mild East Coast weather keeping buyers in New York relaxed, while high sulphur in the U.S. Gulf seemed well supported.

"There's no impetus for the buyers in the East because of the weather, but high sulphurs in the Gulf are better supported," said one cash trader, noting firmer crude and Gulf Coast bunker prices coupled with rumors of more Mexican high sulphur interest helped underpin USG values.
But traders said mild East Coast temperatures this week and competitive East Coast city gate gas prices continued to cut into utility fuel oil burns up and down the region.
In New York Harbor, physical one percent was unchanged at about $16.25 a barrel, with August one percent paper up slightly to the $16.30 area with firmer crude.
NYH 0.3 percent high pour also held steady at about $17.50, helped by a New York utility's contract program for August which was reported to be about 850,000 barrels.
High sulphurs in New York slipped slightly, with 2.2 percent now pegged on either side of $15, traders said.
At the U.S. Gulf, prices were stable, with three percent still at $14.50-75 and one percent at $15.25-50.
A trader said 45-50,000 barrels of prompt USG high quality 2.8 percent sold in the $14.50-60 area, with another high sulphur deal reported earlier at $15.10 (FOB Houston).
A USG one percent deal reportedly at $15.75 for about 100,000 barrels was considered by some above market.

New York city gate August gas prices held relatively steady Wednesday in the low-$2.40s/mmBtu, or $15.25 a barrel equivalent. August gas at Henry Hub, the NYMEX delivery point, was pegged at $2.19/mmBtu, or $13.80 a barrel.
